name: Pan-Africanism
summary: A movement for the solidarity and unity of Africans and people of African descent, opposing slavery, colonialism, racism and neocolonialism. It seeks political and economic integration of the continent, collective self-reliance and recognition of a shared cultural heritage; in its Nkrumahist form it was socialist, and today it is expressed through the African Union.
scope: The mainstream tradition from the Pan-African Congresses through Nkrumah's continental-union socialism (Nkrumaism) to the African Union's Agenda 2063. It excludes Garveyite separatism and Afrocentrism as distinct strands. Most social and economic answers are low-confidence inferences because the movement has no single programme.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity of Africans across colonial borders is the defining aim of Pan-Africanism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Adherents prize continental unity and a shared identity; minority-autonomy questions within states are not addressed, so adherents are split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora Pan-Africanists such as Garvey backed return to Africa, but the mainstream stresses equal rights and anti-racism wherever Africans live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nkrumah drew on Marxism and saw social change as rooted in economic relations and class; inferred from his socialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Nkrumah attacked foreign monopolies and concentrated capital as tools of neo-colonialism; an antitrust stance is inferred, not stated.

no-bailouts.rationale: Nkrumah's socialism favoured state direction of the economy, so public rescue of key firms is not opposed in principle; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses the rule of law and independent institutions, so unchecked majority rule is inferred to be rejected.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Agenda 2063 sets full gender equality and parity in public life as an explicit goal.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nkrumah called for collective continental self-reliance and economic independence but not autarky; a closed bloc with colonies is inferred as rejected.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses decent work and environmental sustainability, so binding standards are inferred to be welcome.

moral-incentives.rationale: Nkrumah's socialism stressed communal duty and consciencist values over private gain; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Nkrumah backed armed liberation struggles but built his own movement through non-violent Positive Action; adherents are split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Nkrumah's egalitarian socialism and his opposition to chiefly privilege imply opposition to inherited rank; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Pan-Africanism asserts a shared African heritage and calls for African history to be taught from an African standpoint, against colonial narratives.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose in opposition to colonialism and the 'civilizing mission' and Nkrumah condemned neo-colonial rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: The movement stresses pride in African identity and unity, and Nkrumah promoted nation-building education; inferred, as loyalty to Africa rather than a single nation is the focus.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Redress for the legacy of slavery and colonialism is central, so adherents would likely accept race-conscious remedies; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Nkrumah's state-led socialism and calls for an African central bank imply public control of money; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nkrumah argued neo-colonial capitalism is imperialism's last stage and bound to fail, but the AU today accepts markets; the answer is mild.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nkrumah condemned neo-colonialism, the exercise of influence by former imperial powers over Africa.

delink-world-market.rationale: Nkrumah favoured self-reliance and continental integration, while the AU's Agenda 2063 seeks greater trade integration; adherents are split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Nkrumah described a global imperial system, but the movement has no settled view on whether rich-country workers are exploited; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement opposes racism and discrimination and sees anti-discrimination law as an essential protection.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The AU's Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights supports written rights, though Nkrumah himself favoured strong executive power; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pan-Africanism rejects the colonial partition of Africa, and the AU treats the inherited borders as a problem for unity; inferred from its anti-colonial stance.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's commitment to democracy and elections; no stated line on hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on continental unity and majority rule over separatism.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's rule-of-law and democratic governance aspirations; Nkrumah himself, though, was a one-party-state ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Agenda 2063 values democratic institutions and parliaments, including the Pan-African Parliament; no stated stance on monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the humanist and communal values in Nkrumah's socialism; not a movement demand.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed by Pan-African sources, and adherents are split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Nkrumah's African socialism stresses communal duty and egalitarian care for the less fortunate.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Pan-Africanism is activist and aims at collective political liberation, so withdrawal is contrary to its aims.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Nkrumah and neo-colonial analyses describe cultural domination as sustaining the colonial order; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's analysis that neocolonialism works through culture, education and institutions as well as force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Nkrumah's neo-colonialism thesis holds that foreign capital drains African resources to the rich world.

native-born-offices.rationale: Pan-Africanism opposes the narrow nationalism of the colonial states and favours continental citizenship; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Nkrumah promoted a distinct African road to socialism, free from direction by other countries' parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Nkrumah and Agenda 2063 stress collective self-reliance, though Agenda 2063 also seeks partnerships; mixed with aid dependency criticism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-Africanism favours keeping inherited borders and unity over redrawing them, and the OAU/AU upheld colonial borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's affirmation of African peoples against colonial rule; not about pre-colonial descendants over settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-racism and its anti-colonial opposition to fascist imperialism; no stated constitutional position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Nkrumah's socialism and anti-imperialism are in tension with the equation of communism with fascism; adherents often reject the equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Pan-Africanism, with its focus on the history of slavery and racism, does not treat slavery as incidental to the Civil War; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to colonial symbols; Africans have toppled colonial statues.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's gender-equality and youth aspirations; not a defining position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; Agenda 2063 calls for ending violence against women, but the question is not a movement issue.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Pan-Africanism holds that African societies should develop their own institutions rather than copy the West; Nkrumah called for African forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nkrumah's coup-wary one-party rule and Agenda 2063 both favour civilian control; the AU rejects military coups.

paid-care-work.rationale: Agenda 2063 calls for gender equality, and recognising unpaid care work is consistent with it; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from African communal values stressing obligations across generations; not a programmatic demand.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the AU programme favours democratic, participatory government over examination-selected officials.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nkrumah's neo-colonialism thesis treats foreign capital control of key sectors as a threat to sovereignty.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's emphasis on gender equality and individual rights; the movement has no position on divorce law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Adherents are split: Nkrumahist one-party mass democracy leaned toward party discipline, while the AU mainstream uses ordinary representative government.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's socialism and state-led development, which favour collective provision over private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's communalism, which draws on traditional communal land holding, though the AU mainstream accepts private tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the AU's democratic commitments in Agenda 2063, which imply legislative oversight of spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Adherents are split: Nkrumah backed English as a common language and Swahili was proposed for the continent, yet Agenda 2063 celebrates linguistic and cultural diversity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-neocolonial concern with foreign control of African resources; the AU mainstream is more open.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-racism and critique of structural colonial legacies; it never addressed disparate-impact doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's socialist critique of capitalist acquisitiveness and the emphasis on communal values.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nkrumah's government and the Organisation of African Unity's Liberation Committee supported liberation movements against colonial and white-minority regimes.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Pan-Africanism upholds African sovereignty and non-interference, and Agenda 2063 stresses African self-determination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Nkrumah's analysis of neocolonialism targets the power of foreign monopoly capital over African governments.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: neocolonialism critics see foreign-funded influence as a threat to sovereignty.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: African socialism stressed full employment and state-led development.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; the movement is more concerned with imperialism than with regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: anti-colonial tradition stresses obedience to legitimate national and continental law, but also resistance to colonial law.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: it opposes external intervention in Africa but supports African Union intervention and anti-colonial solidarity.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the movement is anti-racist and solidarity-based.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; African socialism upholds the family and customary marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: Agenda 2063 stresses good governance, accountability and transparency.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: self-reliance and regional integration in Nkrumah's and Agenda 2063's programme favour local and continental production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: it works through formal bodies such as the African Union and Pan-African Congresses.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: it seeks a continental union with supranational authority above states, not national supremacy.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: Pan-Africanism unites Africans across religions and defines the community by shared heritage.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Its core is opposition to colonialism and neocolonialism, which rules out tributary submission to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its continental unity and shared-development aims; the AU agenda stresses pooled resources and integration.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's African socialism, which keeps personal property while favouring communal and state ownership of major production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Nkrumahist Pan-Africanism was socialist and non-aligned, so it did not seek to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred; Nkrumahists favoured state provision while the AU's present programme accepts mixed delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Nkrumah held that African communal values blend traditional, Islamic and Christian elements and did not call religion an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nkrumah saw capitalism as the root of colonial exploitation, yet the AU embraces market growth; adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses gender equality and Nkrumahist socialism ties emancipation to economic change; not a defining claim.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred; Agenda 2063 stresses gender equality and social services but sets no position on socialising housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Agenda 2063 values African languages and culture, but the movement uses colonial languages and has no purge agenda.

treaties-binding.rationale: No documented position on treaties with nations within borders.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nkrumah's African socialism draws on traditional communalism, though it favoured a state-led rather than small-commune order.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its anti-racism and its opposition to colonial settlement policies.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: African socialism claimed a distinctively African path based on communal values, distinct from both Western capitalism and Soviet communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Pan-Africanism asserts a shared African heritage and a claim to the continent against colonial rule, but it has no doctrine ranking ancestral ties above current inhabitants; this is inferred from its anti-colonial stance.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Pan-Africanism, a movement against racism and racial oppression, has no stated position on the Holocaust; denial is inferred to be rejected as incompatible with its anti-racist aims.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The movement has no programme on sexuality and African governments within the African Union are divided; the answer is a weak inference from its rights and anti-colonial framing, which also treats such laws as colonial legacies.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nkrumah's own Ghana restricted opposition, but Agenda 2063 stresses democracy, human rights and the rule of law; adherents are split and the answer rests on the AU's stated aspirations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Pan-Africanism is not a religious doctrine and Agenda 2063 stresses rights and rule of law; punishing blasphemy is inferred to be foreign to it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Pan-Africanism arose in opposition to colonialism and neocolonialism, which Nkrumah analysed as the exploitation of colonies for the benefit of the imperial power.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The movement is secular and continental rather than Islamic and has no doctrine on this; inferred as split, since it backs resistance to invasion but not a religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Pan-Africanism has no religious-law test of legitimacy; legitimacy in Agenda 2063 comes from democratic governance, so removal by force on this ground is inferred to be rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Agenda 2063 calls for people-driven development and an Africa where citizens take part in governance, and African socialism stressed communal decision-making; not a defining demand.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Pan-Africanism ties racism, colonialism and economic exploitation together, but it does not adopt the intersectional framework on sexism; adherents differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement has no programme on gender identity and many African adherents and governments are hostile or silent; Agenda 2063's gender equality goals concern women and girls, so this is an inference.

assisted-dying.rationale: The movement never addressed assisted dying and has no principle that settles it; adherents are inferred to be split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nkrumahist Pan-Africanism was explicitly socialist while the African Union spans many political tendencies; there is no stated view on the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Nkrumah's African socialism criticised capitalist exploitation, but the movement does not use the Marxist concept of alienation; split between its socialist and mainstream strands.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Pan-Africanism has no position on Islam and Western societies, but its solidarity with Africans and people of African descent worldwide, including Muslims, and its anti-racism are inferred to reject this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Agenda 2063 grounds legitimacy in citizens and democratic governance; the movement is secular in its politics, so this is inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The movement has no stated view on religious dress in state institutions; this is a matter for each state and adherents are inferred to be split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The movement has no programme on employment contracts or harassment claims; adherents are inferred to be indifferent.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nkrumahists favoured state-led socialism, while the African Union's Agenda 2063 accepts mixed economies with markets and social protection; adherents are split between the strands.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nkrumah proposed a continental High Command and Agenda 2063 aims at a peaceful, secure Africa with its own defence capacity; abolition is inferred to be rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Pan-Africanism stresses collective self-reliance and continental integration, and Nkrumah condemned the uneven development imposed by neocolonialism; uneven growth by design is inferred to be rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nkrumah championed positive neutrality and non-alignment, and the Pan-African movement was prominent in the Non-Aligned Movement against Cold War blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Pan-Africanism grew out of opposition to colonial rule and Nkrumah and the AU favour republican, elected government, so hereditary rule of a state is alien to it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nkrumah-style African socialism favoured state and cooperative finance, but the movement has no stated position on mutual credit banks; inferred only.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposing neocolonialism includes resisting external financial control, and Nkrumah attacked lender-imposed conditions as neo-colonial domination.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement fought colonial rule on the principle of self-determination for all Africans, and Agenda 2063 stresses inclusive democratic governance, which rules out wealth qualifications for voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the socialist and anti-oppression strands, which oppose exploitation of both people and land; the movement does not address the link directly.

reification.rationale: Nkrumahist writing drew on Marxist ideas, but reification is not a Pan-African concept and adherents would be split; inferred only.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nkrumahist socialism criticised capitalist and foreign control of media and the economy; inferred from that critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Agenda 2063 calls for the rule of law, independent judiciary and good governance; inferred from this.

racial-franchise.rationale: Pan-Africanism rests on solidarity of all Africans and the fight against racism; Agenda 2063 aspires to a continent of shared citizenship, opposed to racial exclusion from politics.

online-participation.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses technology and citizen participation in governance; online participation is inferred from this, not stated.

open-government-data.rationale: Agenda 2063 calls for transparent, accountable institutions; open records is an inference from that.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement is built on unity across religions as well as ethnicities; restriction of interfaith marriage is not part of it and would cut against unity; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Pan-Africanism stresses solidarity of all Africans across divisions, so boycotting people on religious grounds contradicts its core.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Pan-Africanism has no stated position on sortition; the AU's Agenda 2063 stresses participatory, people-driven governance but through conventional institutions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Pan-Africanism is a secular political movement that celebrates African spiritual heritage without taking a side on reforming religious doctrine; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's socialist critique of capitalist exploitation; not a defining demand.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no stated view and adherents are split between African and diaspora positions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: African socialism and Agenda 2063 draw on African cultural and religious heritage, so state atheism promotion is not part of it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its focus on state-led development rather than abolitionist politics; no source states a view.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's stress on inclusion and unity across Africa's many ethnic communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Nkrumahist preference for state-led socialist provision over private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's aspiration to good governance and democratic values.

vote-delegation.rationale: No stated position; the movement is silent on delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: No stated position; the movement is silent on existential risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between religious traditions.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's aspiration to full gender equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Agenda 2063's continental integration and free movement of Africans.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; Agenda 2063 stresses innovation but nothing on patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not a defining issue for the movement; some Nkrumahist governments ran youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's anti-neocolonialism and African sovereignty.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's opposition to neocolonialism and foreign control.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to slavery and colonialism; recognition of such crimes is a common demand.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Nkrumahist Pan-Africanism is socialist and rooted in communalism, which rejects reward for ownership alone.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the movement's support for armed liberation struggles.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's claim of a shared cultural heritage; applying to nations is contested.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the honouring of liberation heroes.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Nkrumah's thought is materialist and political; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ties to the diaspora, which Agenda 2063 treats as part of Africa.

culture-before-state.rationale: Nkrumah put political independence and union before cultural revival; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Pan-African inclusiveness across peoples.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from continental union taking priority over ethnic units and respect for inherited borders.

independent-unions.rationale: Nkrumah's Ghana brought unions under the ruling party, while Agenda 2063 stresses democracy; mixed, with no common line.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nkrumah's socialism stresses class struggle and egalitarian African communalism, though it never required workers' rule specifically.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nkrumaist socialism favours public control of essentials; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: No stated position; Agenda 2063 takes no line on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Nkrumah favoured state-led industrial projects, not local community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement seeks continental political union with central institutions, so assemblies-only confederalism is a poor fit; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: No stated position; African socialism stresses communal values but not family wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: No stated position; Agenda 2063 aims at healthy citizens without addressing regulation.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No stated position; Nkrumah's concern with foreign financial control gives mixed pulls.

online-anonymity.rationale: No stated position; Agenda 2063 stresses democracy and rights but not online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses democracy, human rights and the dignity of citizens, which implies the person is not a mere means; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Agenda 2063 stresses a shared cultural heritage and values alongside material development; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The AU programme urges integration without a stated view on regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between self-reliance in agriculture and wariness of foreign firms.

dense-cities.rationale: No stated position; Agenda 2063 pairs urbanisation with other goals.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Pan-Africanism rests on the solidarity of Africans and people of African descent, who share interests in resisting racism and colonialism.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in African heritage and identity, against colonial denigration, is central to the movement.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nkrumah backed liberation struggles, including armed ones, but the AU programme stresses peace; adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Africanism unites peoples across the continent regardless of language, and the African Union upholds existing borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: continental unity and Nkrumah's nation-building aims run against separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nkrumah's Neo-Colonialism describes foreign powers balkanising Africa to keep it weak, a core claim of the movement.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: Agenda 2063 stresses an education and skills revolution, and Nkrumahist socialism favours state-provided education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Agenda 2063 stresses environmental sustainability and climate resilience, but no stance on taxation is documented.

future-generations.rationale: Agenda 2063 sets an aspiration of environmentally sustainable, climate-resilient economies.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: Agenda 2063 stresses women's equality and participation, but does not claim distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: Agenda 2063 aims at a peaceful continent, though Nkrumah also sought a continental military command.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: no stated position on secret treaties; Nkrumah criticised neocolonial agreements but did not articulate open diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: Nkrumah argued for state direction of the economy against foreign capital, seen as neocolonialism's tool.

missingStatements.text: Countries of a continent should unite under a single continental government.
missingStatements.rationale: Nkrumah envisioned a union government of Africa and the AU pursues political integration.

notes: Strands differ: Nkrumahists are socialist and favour union government; the AU mainstream is democratic and market-friendly; Garveyites emphasise return and separatism.
